focus: Quote the card's own 'Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu' and give the unreal-past pairing in plain words, not tense-name jargon.
Salvage only 'Tu devrais' = 'you should' – devoir in conditional gives advice; kill the backticked endings table and the off-card voudrais bit.
Quote 'la plus belle ville que j'aie jamais visitée' – superlative + que triggers subjunctive aie, not ai.
Card has ONE pronoun, not two – the real point: positive imperative puts the pronoun after the verb with a hyphen: Explique-lui.
Anchor on the card's 'Réfléchis' keeping its -s (only -er verbs drop it); drop the off-card 'Finis tes devoirs' example.
Keep the register fact (aller + infinitive is the everyday spoken future) but quote the card's 'vont repeindre', strip backticks and off-card examples.
Use the card's exact 'Si tu lui parlais... il comprendrait' for the fixed si + imparfait / conditional pairing; drop the paraphrased example.
Real trap: no a or de between aller and the infinitive, unlike English 'going TO'. Quote 'va commander'; strip backticks and fix 'three parts'.
Anchor on 'aimerait' = would like – conditional softens a wish; drop the off-card cafe-ordering voudrais material.
Pick one rule: 'que' replaces the object (j'ai lu le livre becomes le livre que j'ai lu); the agreement note is invisible on masculine 'lu' – cut it.
Use the card's own 'Si j'avais le permis, je conduirais' for conditional-as-unreal-present; drop the off-card drinking example.
Make the agreement visible: recu stays bare after 'le cadeau', but a feminine noun would force recue – show that contrast, anchored in the card.
Anchor on the card's 'Tu verras' = you'll see (reassurance); 'on verra' may stay only as a one-line sibling example.
Quote 'Si tu etudies... tu reussiras' – present after si, future in the main clause; contrast with quand/des que, which DO take the future.
